text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp posted another sharp fourth-quarter and full-year loss in 1996, but chief executive officer Peter Willmott said the television and video products company is moving in the right direction.
"We're making progress toward putting the company on a much sounder (financial) footing," Willmott said in a telephone interview.
Earlier, Zenith reported a loss for the fourth quarter of $1.05 a share after $40.0 million in restructuring and other charges, compared with a loss of $0.42 a year ago.
For 1996, it posted a loss of $2.73 a share after about $80 million in charges, compared with a loss of $1.85 a share a year ago.

"It's been a rough period, but we sense we're moving forward," Willmott added, but declined to predict when Zenith would return to profitability. The last time Glenview, Ill.-based Zenith posted a full year of profit was in 1988.
Kalb, Voorhis & Co analyst Robert Gutenstein said he sees Zenith moving back into the black "sometime in the latter half of the year."
"With new plant automation and a higher-margin picture tube coming into the product line, Zenith's chances of profitability are improved," Gutenstein said.

Willmott said Zenith is working on new product introductions, including enhancements to its television line and its new NetVision product linking TVs to the Internet, which will be introduced during the second half of 1997.

He said he expects the company to complete new financing needed to support its capital requirements "within the month." LG Electronics Inc, its majority shareholder, will be guarantor on some of the financing, he noted.
"This will amount to a total redo of our balance sheet," he said, adding that the financing package could be as large as $400 million, in both new and replacement funding.

Meanwhile, Willmott said the company will have sufficient manufacturing capacity for 1997. He said new equipment being installed at the company's Melrose Park, Ill. plant for production of computer monitors should be operable by the middle of the second quarter.
The company is planning a multi-million dollar advertising campaign that is expected to capitalize on Zenith's brand name recognition.

In another cost-cutting move, Willmott also said distribution of Zenith products will be assumed by LG Electronics in Canada and Mexico. "We think they'll do a good job selling our products," he said.
